title: Overview
use_cases: Use when developing collaborative creative writing workflows using small open-source models
Implement when single-pass LLM generation produces predictable or low-novelty narratives
Configure when simulating human writers' room dynamics for iterative storytelling
Use when balancing narrative creativity with structural coherence through feedback loops
Implement when evaluating the efficacy of MFER or RFM frameworks against single-agent baselines
content: Self-adapting multi-agent AI systems in creative writing are ensembles of specialized large language models (LLMs) that collaboratively generate and iteratively refine short-form narratives through structured feedback loops among distinct agent roles.[1] These systems emerged to address key limitations of conventional single-pass LLM generation, which tends to produce coherent but predictable outputs due to its reliance on high-probability token sampling, often stifling novel creative directions. By simulating the collaborative dynamics of a human writers' room—where professionals engage in brainstorming, idea sharing, critical judgment, and repeated revision—these multi-agent frameworks enable iterative collective refinement that balances creativity with coherence and relevance.[1] The approach has been notably applied to flash fiction generation using small open-source LLMs, such as Llama-2-7B and Zephyr-1.6B, which offer greater accessibility and efficiency compared to larger proprietary models. Representative frameworks include the Reiterative Feedback Mechanism (RFM), Modular Feedback-Enhanced Revision (MFER), and Mixture of Experts-Inspired MFER (MOE-MFER), each demonstrating how targeted agent interactions and multiple refinement passes can enhance narrative quality beyond baseline single-agent methods.[1]
